reasoning: Both attempts are functional and secure. A wins because its bookkeeping stays correct however a block is destroyed (the Destroying hook), its RemoveBlock does a proper IsA check, and its comments are fewer and accurate. B is solid, but its cooldown comment misdescribes the code, a block destroyed outside RemoveBlock leaves stale state behind, and it adds banner and header noise.

criteria.note: Both remotes and the PlacedBlocks folder are created, the cap and the os.clock cooldown are enforced, PlayerRemoving clears all state, and `part.Destroying` → `forgetBlock` keeps the counts right even when a block is destroyed some other way.

RemoveBlock checks `typeof(block) ~= "Instance" or not block:IsA("BasePart")` and then `ownerByBlock[block] ~= player` before destroying anything; blockType and position are passed as unknown into PlacementRules.validate.

The comments on server-only ownership versus the OwnerUserId attribute, the Destroying hook, and the ownerByBlock rejection each add something the code can't show; the 'keep this quiet' note is marginal.
There are few comments, each short and placed next to the line it governs, with no banners or block-end markers.

criteria.criterion: No change history or request references
criteria.note: The comments describe the code as it stands; 'for the client UI' describes a consumer of the attribute, not the request.
It uses BlockTypes.STYLES and PlacementRules.BLOCK_SIZE/validate, is strictly typed, contains no client code, and passes all checks.

Remotes, folder, cap via `#blocks`, cooldown, and leave cleanup all work, and the PlayerAdded gating plus the GetPlayers loop are solid; a block destroyed outside RemoveBlock leaves stale entries in blocks and ownerByBlock, so it keeps counting toward the cap.
It checks `typeof(block) ~= "Instance"` and owner lookup before destroying, which is safe, but it casts `block :: BasePart` without an IsA check and checks `typeof(result)` on validate's output.
The PlayerAdded/PlayerRemoving lifetime comment is good, but 'Only accepted requests reset the cooldown' is misleading, because requests later rejected by the cap or by validation also reset it.
There are many top-level `-- SERVICES --` style banners, an author/date/description header, and two-line comments that could be shorter.

criteria.criterion: No change history or request references
criteria.note: No history or references to the request appear.
It reuses BlockTypes and PlacementRules through `@game` requires, is typed, contains no client code, and passes the checks.

strengths: Bookkeeping stays correct no matter how a block gets destroyed (Destroying hook)
RemoveBlock does a full IsA check plus an ownership check
weaknesses: A request that arrives after a player has left could recreate lastPlaceTime state (a minor leak)
Keeps a separate blockCount when the size of the set could be derived instead

strengths: Explicit per-player lifetime keyed to PlayerAdded and PlayerRemoving, including players already in the game
weaknesses: The cooldown comment doesn't match the code's behavior
Blocks destroyed by other means stay in the per-player list and count toward the cap
